hook.text: A patient has a headache. It could be a brain tumor. Or he stayed up all night drinking coffee.

buildup.text: William of Ockham wrote in the 1300s: do not multiply entities beyond necessity. Simpler explanations come first.

discovery.text: Occam's Razor does not say simple is always right. It says start with the simplest explanation and test from there.

twist.text: Conspiracy theories violate Occam's Razor constantly. They require dozens of actors to secretly coordinate perfectly.

climax.text: The razor is a starting point, not a verdict. Simple first, complex only when evidence demands it.

punchline.text: Start simple. Add complexity only when forced.

quiz.question: What does Occam's Razor actually recommend?
options: The simplest answer is always correct
Start with the simplest explanation and only add complexity when evidence requires it
